findings.title: New abstract interface method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `int order()` is added to the public `CryptoProvider` interface as an abstract method with no default. Any third-party or out-of-tree implementation stops compiling, or throws AbstractMethodError at runtime when CryptoIntegration sorts the providers. Declaring it as a default method (for example returning 0) would keep compatibility.

findings.title: Providers with equal order are silently chosen nondeterministically
findings.body: The old code failed fast when multiple providers were found. The new code sorts by order and picks the first one, logging the rest only at debug level. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. If two of them end up on the classpath, for example FIPS plus default, the one selected depends on ServiceLoader iteration order. This can silently run Keycloak in non-FIPS mode. The code should still throw when the top two providers have the same order.

findings.title: Indefinite length (-1) not rejected
findings.body: `readLength` returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding. `readNext` then computes a wrong length, and `readInteger` calls `new byte[-1]`, which throws NegativeArraySizeException instead of IOException. A malformed signature can therefore surface as an unexpected runtime exception rather than a verification failure.

findings.title: Dead encoder calls
findings.body: Lines 114-115 build two ASN1Encoder objects and throw them away. This is wasted work and should be removed.
